title: Separating Mixtures: Adding a Force
subtitle: When waiting is not enough, bring wind, water, magnets or a machine.
objectives: Explain how winnowing separates by weight using moving air
Explain how panning uses density and flowing water
Explain what magnetic separation can and cannot pick out
Explain how a centrifuge speeds up settling
Match a mixture to the method that exploits the right difference

cards.title: Last week you waited. This week you push
cards.text: Gravity alone is slow and sometimes useless. Add moving air, moving water, a magnet or a spin, and the same sorting happens faster.

cards.title: Moving air sorts by weight
cards.text: Throw a mixture of light and heavy pieces into a breeze. The light ones travel; the heavy ones drop.
points: **Rice and chaff** is the classic: the husk blows away, the grain lands.
**It uses weight and air resistance**, not size.
**Done here for centuries** with a flat basket and a windy afternoon.
**No wind?** Make some.

cards.title: Moving air sorts by weight
cards.alt: Rice being winnowed on a round woven tray, light chaff blowing off the edge while the grain stays
cards.text: Heavy grain stays in the bilao. Light chaff leaves. No sieve involved.

cards.title: Five buttons
cards.text: Tap each method. The second line names the force actually doing the work.

cards.title: An electric fan is a winnowing machine
cards.text: Point a fan at a tray of mixed light and heavy pieces and you have made a wind on demand.
points: **The blade is pitched**, so turning it pushes air forward.
**A flat blade** would slice the air and move almost none of it.
**Speed settings** change how hard the wind blows, so how light a piece must be to move.
**Industrial winnowers** are exactly this, scaled up.

question.explain: Light pieces are carried by the air; heavy ones fall straight down.

cards.title: Flowing water sorts by density
cards.text: Swirl sand and water in a shallow pan. The light material washes over the edge and the dense stays.
points: **Gold is about seven times denser** than ordinary sand.
**So it sinks fast** while sand is still being carried.
**The swirl keeps lifting** the light material so the water can take it.
**Density, not size.** A big light grain still goes.

cards.title: A magnet picks by material, not by size
cards.text: This is the only method this week that asks what something is made of rather than how heavy it is.
points: **Iron, nickel and cobalt** respond. Most metals do not.
**Aluminium is a metal** and a magnet ignores it completely.
**Scrapyards use huge ones** to pull steel out of mixed waste.
**It works dry or wet**, and through a container.

question.text: A magnet will separate aluminium cans from plastic.
question.explain: Aluminium is not magnetic. A magnet would pull neither — you would need a different difference.

cards.title: The magnet hiding in your sump plug
cards.text: Many engines have a magnetic drain plug. It is there to collect the metal the engine sheds as it wears.
points: **Fine steel particles** come off gears and bearings.
**The magnet holds them** instead of letting them circulate.
**A mechanic reads it.** Glitter is normal; chunks are not.
**Separation as a warning light**, not just a clean-up.

cards.title: A centrifuge is gravity, turned up
cards.text: Spin something fast and the contents feel a force many times stronger than their own weight.
points: **Settling that takes hours** finishes in minutes.
**Blood is spun** to split cells from plasma.
**A washing machine spin cycle** is this, separating water from cloth.
**Nothing new is happening** — it is sedimentation, hurried.

question.text: What does a centrifuge actually change?
options: It makes settling happen far faster
It heats the mixture until it splits
question.explain: Same separation as leaving it standing, but the spin supplies a much stronger pull.

cards.title: A blood test starts with a spin
cards.text: The tube goes into a centrifuge before anyone looks at it, because the parts have to be apart first.
points: **Red cells pack to the bottom**, being densest.
**Plasma sits on top**, straw-coloured, not red.
**A thin layer between** is the white cells.
**Left on a bench** it would do this anyway, just far slower.

terms.def: Using moving air to carry light pieces away from heavy ones.
Using swirling water to wash light material off a dense one.
Pulling out iron, nickel or cobalt with a magnet.
A machine that spins a mixture so settling happens much faster.
How much mass is packed into a given volume.

cards.title: Only one thing in the dish is iron
cards.alt: A bar magnet lifting dark iron filings in spikes out of a dish of pale sand
cards.text: The sand is untouched. Magnetism is a separating force that ignores everything else.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Winnowing uses weight and air. Panning uses density and water.
A magnet is the one method that asks what a thing is made of.
A centrifuge does not do anything new. It hurries gravity.
Pick the method that exploits the biggest difference you have.

quiz.explain: Moving air carries the light pieces; the heavy ones fall.
quiz.objective: Explain how winnowing separates by weight using moving air

quiz.text: Panning for gold works because gold is…
quiz.explain: Gold is roughly seven times denser than sand, so it sinks while sand washes away.
quiz.objective: Explain how panning uses density and flowing water

quiz.text: A magnet will pick up which of these?
quiz.explain: Iron, nickel and cobalt respond. Aluminium and copper are metals but not magnetic.
quiz.objective: Explain what magnetic separation can and cannot pick out

quiz.text: A centrifuge separates things that would never separate on their own.
quiz.explain: It speeds up settling that gravity would do eventually. It does not create a new separation.
quiz.objective: Explain how a centrifuge speeds up settling

quiz.text: Why does a blood sample go in a centrifuge first?
options: To separate cells from plasma quickly
quiz.explain: Red cells pack at the bottom and plasma sits above, in minutes rather than hours.
quiz.objective: Explain how a centrifuge speeds up settling

quiz.text: Why can an electric fan be used for winnowing?
options: Its pitched blades make a steady wind on demand
quiz.explain: The blade is a twisted wing. Turning it pushes air forward, which is all winnowing needs.
quiz.objective: Explain how winnowing separates by weight using moving air

quiz.text: You have a mixture of sand and iron filings. Best method?
quiz.explain: Iron is magnetic and sand is not. That is the biggest and cleanest difference available.
quiz.objective: Match a mixture to the method that exploits the right difference

quiz.text: What is a magnetic sump plug in an engine for?
options: To collect worn steel particles from the oil
quiz.explain: It catches the fine steel the engine sheds, and a mechanic reads what has collected.
quiz.objective: Explain what magnetic separation can and cannot pick out

quiz.text: Panning separates by size, so a large grain always stays in the pan.
quiz.explain: Panning sorts by density. A large light grain washes out; a small dense one stays.
quiz.objective: Explain how panning uses density and flowing water

quiz.text: A washing machine's spin cycle is most like which method?
quiz.explain: It spins fast so water is flung out of the cloth — settling, hurried by spin.
quiz.objective: Explain how a centrifuge speeds up settling

quiz.text: Which method asks what a material is made of rather than how heavy it is?
quiz.explain: Only the magnet cares about the substance. The rest work on weight or density.
quiz.objective: Match a mixture to the method that exploits the right difference

quiz.text: Rice mixed with its light husk is best separated by…
quiz.explain: The husk is far lighter, so moving air carries it off and the grain drops.
quiz.objective: Match a mixture to the method that exploits the right difference

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 3 Science, the second week the scope gives to separating heterogeneous mixtures. Week 2 covered the methods that need only gravity; this one covers the four that add something — moving air, moving water, a magnet, a spin. The organising question is which difference each method exploits, because that is what an exam item is really asking. The magnet is set apart deliberately as the only method that asks what a thing is made of, and the aluminium case is tested, since 'metal means magnetic' is the usual error.
discussion: Which difference is each method using?
Why does a magnet ignore an aluminium can?
What is a centrifuge actually adding?
extension: Winnow a bowl of rice and torn paper with a desk fan on its lowest setting.
Run a magnet through dry sand with iron filings stirred in, inside a plastic bag so it stays clean.
misconceptions: That all metals are magnetic. Only iron, nickel and cobalt, and alloys of them.
That panning sorts by size. It sorts by density.
That a centrifuge does something gravity cannot. It only does it faster.
